what: When porting Taprats algorithms, separate the "algorithmic" core (the geometric decision: which edge to split, where faces close, which crossings count) from the "busy-work" (iterating, index juggling, keeping vectors sorted, threading state). Express the busy-work with standard functional tools (Enum.reduce/map/reduce_while, threading the map through), and keep the algorithmic part in small named pure functions. Restructuring the Java's control flow to do this is expected.
why: The user's direction during Plan 1b brainstorming (2026-10-20). Mutate-in-place code does not survive a literal port, and the separation also gives the workbench's step sequences their natural labels.
